scheme: USDA quality grades (carcass beef, young cattle)
levels: Prime; Choice; Select; Standard; Commercial; Utility; Cutter; Canner (steer/heifer/cow). Bullock class: Prime; Choice; Select; Standard; Utility
note: Driven by marbling (Prime min slightly abundant; Choice min small; Standard practically devoid) plus maturity. Voluntary fee-for-service. Principal retail grades are Prime, Choice, Select

scheme: USDA yield grades
levels: Yield Grade 1; 2; 3; 4; 5 (1 = leanest, highest cutability)
note: Estimates usable lean meat from fat thickness over ribeye, ribeye area and kidney/pelvic/heart fat. Quality and yield grade stated separately

scheme: JMGA (Japan Meat Grading Association) yield grade x meat quality grade
levels: Yield: A (high), B, C. Meat quality: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 (best first). 15 combinations A5 ... C1
note: Yield grade = ratio of meat to carcass weight. Quality grade from marbling, meat colour and brightness, firmness and texture, fat colour and brightness; the lowest of the four sub-grades becomes the final number. MAFF Wagyu guidebook

scheme: BMS (Beef Marbling Standard), Japan
levels: BMS No. 12 (top) down to No. 1; roughly 8-12 corresponds to quality 5 (A5), 5-7 to 4, 3-4 to 3, 1-2 to quality 1-2
note: Fetched from a commercial exporter page, not JMGA itself; mapping of BMS bands to quality numbers is that page's. Australian marble score 0-9+ and USDA scales are different scales

scheme: USDA consumer grades for shell eggs
levels: U.S. Grade AA; Grade A; Grade B (each with at-origin and at-destination tolerances)
note: Interior and shell quality (air cell, white, yolk, cleanliness); separate from weight class. AA at origin >=87% AA quality; B >=90% B. Weight classes (Jumbo, XL, L, M, S, Peewee) are separate and not on this fetched page

scheme: EU geographical indications and quality schemes
levels: PDO (protected designation of origin: every production stage in the area); PGI (protected geographical indication: at least one stage in area; wine at least 85% grapes from area); GI for spirit drinks; TSG (traditional speciality guaranteed: tradition not place); optional quality term 'mountain product'. Not a ranked scale
note: Single legal framework Regulation (EU) 2024/1143 in force from 13 May 2024 covering wine, spirits and agricultural products. Label mandatory for PDO/PGI/TSG food, optional for wine and spirits

scheme: Label Rouge (France, INAO)
levels: Not a ladder: a single national sign for products of 'superior quality' vs similar standard products; can combine with PGI or TSG but not with PDO/AOP
note: Superior quality rests on sensory characteristics, production conditions, image and presentation; verified by independent certifier and ongoing organoleptic tests vs standard product. Free-range poultry has common production conditions (CPC) page. Specific free-range/heritage-breed criteria not on this fetched page

scheme: MSC Fisheries Standard (wild capture)
levels: Certified / not certified (blue MSC label). Three principles: sustainable fish stocks; minimising environmental impact; effective management. Performance indicators scored 60 minimum, 80 = best practice, 100 = state of the art; certification needs every PI >=60 and average >=80 per principle
note: Voluntary, third-party assessed. Sustainability label rather than a quality grade

scheme: IOC trade standard designations
levels: Extra virgin (free acidity <=0.8 g/100 g); Virgin (<=2.0); Ordinary virgin (<=3.3, in the standard); Lampante virgin (>3.3, not fit for consumption as is); then Refined olive oil (<=0.3); Olive oil = refined + virgin blend (<=1.0); Crude olive pomace oil; Refined olive pomace oil (<=0.3); Olive pomace oil (<=1.0)
note: Classification also needs organoleptic panel (median of defects and fruitiness) and chemical purity criteria; free acidity is only one test. Ordinary virgin appears in trade standard text seen in search results but not on this fetched page

scheme: ISO 3632 saffron categories
levels: Category I (crocin E1% 440nm >=190; picrocrocin >=70; safranal 20-50); Category II (crocin 150-189; picrocrocin 55-69); Category III (crocin 100-149; picrocrocin 40-54)
note: Fetched from a saffron retailer's explainer, not the ISO text (paywalled); thresholds as that page states them. Trade names Sargol, Negin, Pushal, Coupe, Mongra and the US ASTA physical grading sit alongside

scheme: UMF (Unique Manuka Factor) and MGO
levels: UMF 5+ upward by whole numbers; page table gives UMF 10+ = MGO 263, 15+ = 514, 20+ = 829, 24+ = 1122, 26+ = 1282, 28+ = 1450, 30+ = 1620 up to UMF 33 = MGO 1900. MGO is a single-compound mg/kg number
note: Fetched from a retailer, not the UMF Honey Association. UMF tests four markers (MGO, leptosperin, DHA, HMF), only for monofloral manuka from licensed producers

scheme: SCA cupping score bands (100-point scale, Q Grader)
levels: Outstanding 90-100; Excellent 85-89.99; Very Good 80-84.99 (specialty threshold is 80); Very Good (below specialty) 75-79.99; below 75 commercial/commodity (per fnb.tech)
note: Band names from a trade site; other sites label 75-79.99 as not specialty. Official SCA Heritage Standards page (same fetch) gives green-grade rule: zero category 1 defects and at most 5 category 2 defects in 350 g sample, water activity below 0.70 aw. Ten cupping attributes

scheme: SCA green coffee specialty grade rule
levels: Specialty grade / not specialty (zero category-1 defects, <=5 category-2 defects, 350 g sample, aw <0.70)
note: SCA Heritage Standards page; binary pass/fail on physical defects before cupping score

scheme: Orthodox leaf grades (India, Sri Lanka)
levels: Whole leaf, best first: SFTGFOP (SFTGFOP1) > FTGFOP (FTGFOP1) > TGFOP > GFOP > FOP > OP. Then size classes: broken (BOP, FBOP, GBOP, TGFBOP1) > fannings (BOPF) > dust (PD, D1)
note: Grades describe leaf size and tip content, not flavour. '1' suffix = best of batch within grade. CTC uses a separate scale. China uses names plus Grade 1/2/Special; Japan uses other names. Retailer page

scheme: Matcha grades (marketing terms)
levels: Ceremonial grade (first flush, ichibancha, drunk plain as usucha); Culinary grade (later harvest, for lattes and baking); some sellers add Premium between
note: Page states the terms are not regulated by Japanese law; marketing labels. Seller page

scheme: ICCO fine or flavour cocoa vs bulk
levels: Fine (flavour) cocoa vs bulk (ordinary) cocoa; recognised via Annex C of International Cocoa Agreement 2010, with per-country share of exports (e.g. Ecuador 75%, Peru 75%, Madagascar 100%, Trinidad and Tobago 100%, Dominican Republic 60%, Ghana and Cameroon unquantified)
note: Fine flavour about 12% of world exports; generally Criollo/Trinitario vs Forastero with exceptions (Ecuador Nacional). No single universal criterion. Chocolate itself is graded by cocoa percentage and trade names, not an official ladder here

scheme: Italian appellation pyramid
levels: DOCG; DOC; IGT; Vino da Tavola. Extra terms Classico, Superiore, Riserva. EU mapping: DOCG and DOC = PDO (DOP), IGT = PGI (IGP)
note: Counts as of 2025: 78 DOCG, about 329 DOC, over 120 IGT. DOC since 1963, DOCG 1980, IGT 1992. Educational site, not the Italian ministry

scheme: EU marketing standards (Delegated Reg. 2023/2465): quality class and weight grade
levels: Quality: Class A; Class B (downgraded or unmarked within 10 days). Weight (Class A): XL >=73 g; L 63-<73 g; M 53-<63 g; S <53 g
note: Consolidated text of 14 Oct 2024. 'Extra'/'extra fresh' allowed until day 9 after laying

scheme: EU farming-method codes (printed on egg, packs show producer code)
levels: Code 0 organic; 1 free range; 2 barn; 3 enriched cages (best-welfare first)
note: Free range: continuous daytime access to open-air runs; max 2,500 hens per hectare (one per 4 m2). Codes 1-3 table seen in fetched annex; organic code 0 follows Reg. 2018/848 (named on page)

scheme: USDA official grade terms by species (Public Law 272)
levels: Chicken, turkey, duck, goose, rabbit: U.S. Grade A; B; C. Pork: U.S. No. 1; No. 2; No. 3; No. 4; U.S. Utility, but pork is currently not officially graded and may not be labeled by grade. Lamb: Prime; Choice; Good; Utility; Cull. Veal: Prime; Choice; Good; Standard; Utility
note: Marketing terms such as free range, heritage, organic are separate label claims and not grade levels

scheme: Spanish Norma de Calidad del Ibérico (RD 4/2014) colour labels
levels: Black label (100% ibérico de bellota, acorn-fed purebred) > Red (ibérico de bellota) > Green (ibérico cebo de campo) > White (ibérico de cebo, grain-fed). Breed share 100/75/50% stated
note: Wikipedia summary of the royal decree; labels also cover paleta and caña de lomo. Only black label may say pata negra. Bellota hams cured about 36 months, cebo about 24 months

scheme: 'Sashimi grade' / 'sushi grade'
levels: No legal grade. FDA parasite-destruction freezing: -20 C (-4 F) for 7 days, or -35 C until solid then 15 h, or -35 C then -20 C for 24 h
note: Marketing term; fetched from a food-science explainer citing FDA Fish and Fishery Products Hazards and Controls Guidance (FDA page itself not fetched)

scheme: Caviar trade grade labels (no official body)
levels: Grade 1 (000) > Grade 2 (00) > pressed (payusnaya); producer-specific names Imperial, Royal, Reserve; Malossol = low-salt cure not a grade. Egg size by species: Beluga 3.5-4 mm+, Osetra 2.5-3.5, Siberian 2-2.5, Sevruga 1.5-2
note: Seller's guide, states there is no single standardized grading body; criteria egg size, colour uniformity, membrane integrity, aroma, luster

scheme: Comte rating out of 20 and band colour
levels: Green band 'Comte Extra' (over 14 of 20) > brown band (12-14) > below 12 may not carry Comte name. Minimum 4 months ageing, up to 18-24+ months
note: US promotion body page. Colour band says nothing about age. Rating covers taste and appearance

scheme: Consortium selection marks and ageing
levels: Selection at 12 months: passes with Consorzio fire-brand (first category); mezzano (medium-grade) has parallel lines engraved on rind; rejects lose the name. Minimum maturation 12 months (stated as longest of any PDO cheese); market ages 12-18, 22-24, 30-36, 40+ months
note: FAQ confirms 12-month minimum, mezzano, no maximum; most cheese on market 24-36 months. Age bands 12-18/24/30-36/40+ come from the consortium sensory page seen in search results only

scheme: BNIC / AOC Cognac age mentions (youngest eau-de-vie in blend)
levels: VS (2 yrs) < Superior (3) < VSOP (4) < Vieille Reserve (5) < Napoleon (6) < XO / Extra / Hors d'age (10) < XXO (14, added Nov 2018). No exact age statements except vintages
note: Producer (Jean Fillioux) page citing AOC specification and BNIC; older sources give XO as 6 years

scheme: Scotch Whisky Regulations 2009 reg. 12 age statements
levels: No ladder: any age statement must be in years and refer to the youngest component; distillation-year claims need a single year plus bottling year or age
note: Regulation text fetched; 3-year minimum maturation is in other regulations (not fetched). Categories single malt, blended malt, single grain, blended grain, blended

scheme: Japan official rice inspection grade (brown rice)
levels: 1st grade; 2nd grade; 3rd grade; sub-standard; non-standardized (inspected by appearance, moisture, weight per volume, head rice ratio, damage). Separate 'meigara' variety/district price classes 1st-5th
note: 1993 JARQ paper, system since reformed (2016 simplification per other sources); historical but names the grade ladder

scheme: Japan Grain Inspection Association yearly taste ranking
levels: Special A (Tokubetsu A) > A > A' > B > B' relative to a standard Koshihikari blend; six taste attributes
note: Blog summary; panel blind taste test since 1971; Special A not stable year to year
